new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (14 pp., text layer, Word/Acrobat 2001, header 'In Texas linguistic forum 41.. 57-69'). Preprint p. 2, §2 'Data Collection, Experimental Set-up, and Measurement' reads exactly: 'All were controlled for stress: (C)CVV couplets are stressed, and in (C)CVCV couplets, stress falls predictably on the first vowel.' Verbatim match. The other locators also check: p. 7 fn. 2 (continued on p. 8) 'two unstressed vowels which are themselves much shorter than their stressed V1 counterparts'; p. 10 'V1 of (C)CVCV couplets, i.e. on stressed vowels implementing a lexically specified tone target'. No other stress passages in the file (a full-text search for stress/accent per page). Identity: p. 1 'Co…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress falls on the first vowel (first mora) of the couplet, the bimoraic root that is the canonical lexical word: in CVCV couplets on V1, i.e. the penultimate (root-initial) syllable; in CVV couplets the single (long or diphthongal) syllable carries it. Stress is predictable, not lexical. Second-hand (Penner 2019 reporting Gerfen 1996:131), this penultimate stress is supported instrumentally by greater vowel duration and amplitude on the stressed syllable, and Gerfen treats laryngealization as licensed only under stress (on V1).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned in any opened source.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated; stress is described as predictable ('falls predictably on the first vowel'). Penner 2019 (p. 92) notes that other Mixtec varieties show shifts or tone-stress interactions but lists Coatzospan among the plain penultimate-stress descriptions.
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the couplet (the bimoraic root/morpheme, (C)CVV or (C)CVCV), i.e. the lexical word in citation form; the study measured words uttered in isolation. Nothing is said about longer words with affixes or clitics or about phrase-level prominence. The language is tonal (contrastive H/L tone patterns on couplets) with stress independent of tone.
new_statements.identity_note: All sources describe the Mixtec of San Juan Coatzospan (Sierra Mazateca, northern Oaxaca), i.e. coat1241 / ISO miz itself; Gerfen's fieldwork (1993-1997) was in that village. No other variety is involved. WALS code mxz 'Mixtec (Coatzospan)' is the same lect.
